title: Bankfull and Beyond: Identifying Longitudinally Persistent Reach‐Scale River Corridor Features From Topography
content:
Abstract

The dynamic interaction of fluvial processes and channel form creates nested, longitudinally persistent landforms such as bars, river banks, and floodplains that are critical for river corridor characterization and modeling. However, these river corridor features remain difficult to consistently and objectively identify at scale. Here we present a semi-automated, terrain-based approach to identify and map longitudinally persistent landforms using the INFLection-based Elevations from Channel Topography (INFLECT) method. INFLECT identifies the elevation of persistent topographic features based on changes in lateral topographic slope (i.e., inflections) from cross-section geometry, and then aggregates these inflections over cross-sections to represent reach-scale conditions. We apply INFLECT to six total reaches from two rivers with diverse channel forms and compare the results to other lines of evidence including aerial imagery, flow recurrence, and hydraulic modeling. We identify baseflow channels, active channels, top of banks, and floodplains, although not every type of feature is detectable in each reach or each cross-section. Topographic features were most clearly distinguished in alluvial reaches with uniform, well-defined banks and expansive floodplains; however, innovations built into our method also enabled feature identification in highly confined or bedrock channels where topographic features were less continuous or defined. The freely available INFLECT tool enables semi-automated topographic river corridor characterization, with implications for hydrologic research, management, and applications.
